messages.subject: Vertical line at a date
parts:
Suppose for this plot:

Date <- 33817:34016
y1 <- runif(200,20,200)
y2 <- rnorm(200)
library(scales)
library(ggplot2)
library(reshape2)
df <- data.frame(y1,y2,Date)
dfmelt=melt(df,id="Date")
dfmelt$Date = as.Date(dfmelt$Date, origin=('1899-12-30'))
ggplot(dfmelt,aes(x=Date,y=value))+geom_point()+
facet_wrap(~variable,scales = "free_y",ncol=1)+ theme(axis.title.y = element_blank())+
scale_x_date(labels = date_format("%m-%Y"))

that I'd like to put a vertical line in both panels at some critical date, like September 15, 1992.  How would I do that?

David

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Vertical line at a date
parts:
Evidently, even though your dates use a Microsoft Excel origin, when
plotting in ggplot2 with a Date axis, you need to use R's date origin
of 1 Jan 1970, and you need to use the numeric value of the date from
that origin for annotation such as vlines or text. The following gives
you vertical lines in each panel at the same date.

# 8293 days from 1970-01-01 to 1992-09-15
ggplot(dfmelt,aes(x=Date,y=value))+
geom_vline(xintercept = 8293, size = 1,
linetype = "dashed", color = "darkorange") +
geom_point()+
facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "free_y", ncol=1)+
